text: Solomon said to God, “You have shown great faithful love to my father David and have made me king in his place.

The trumpeters and singers joined as one, making one sound of praise and thanksgiving to the LORD. They raised their voices with trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments, praising the LORD: “For he is good; his faithful love lasts forever.” Then a cloud filled the house, the LORD’s house.
He prayed, “LORD, Israel’s God, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth. You keep covenant and faithful love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart.

if they return to you with all their heart and all their being in the land of their captivity, where they have been taken, and pray toward the land you gave their ancestors, the city you chose, and the house I built for your name,
LORD God, do not turn away your anointed one. Remember the faithful love shown to David your servant.”

All the Israelites saw the fire descend and the LORD’s glory over the house. They knelt with their faces to the ground on the pavement, bowed in worship, and thanked the LORD: “For he is good; his faithful love lasts forever.”

The priests stood at their posts. The Levites had the musical instruments for the LORD that King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD—“His faithful love lasts forever”—as David offered praise through them. Opposite them the priests sounded trumpets, and all Israel stood.
and my people, who bear my name, humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
But if you all turn away and abandon the statutes and commands I have set before you, and go off to serve other gods and bow to them,

People will answer, ‘Because they abandoned the LORD, their ancestors’ God, who brought them out of Egypt. They clung to other gods, bowed to them, and served them. That is why he brought all this disaster on them.’”
The king’s ships sailed to Tarshish with Huram’s servants. Once every three years the Tarshish ships returned carrying gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard, he was in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon. Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
But he abandoned the elders’ advice and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.
The king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam abandoned the elders’ advice
‘The LORD says: Do not march out and fight your brothers. Everyone must return home, for this has come from me.’” They listened to the LORD’s words and turned back from marching against Jeroboam.
Jeroboam appointed his own priests for the high places, the goat-demons, and the calves he had made.
People from every tribe of Israel who set their hearts on seeking the LORD, Israel’s God, followed them to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, their ancestors’ God.
Once Rehoboam’s kingdom was established and he had grown strong, he abandoned the LORD’s instruction, and all Israel followed him.

Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and Judah’s officials, who had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak. He told them, “The LORD says: You abandoned me, so I have abandoned you into Shishak’s hand.”
Israel’s officials and the king humbled themselves and said, “The LORD is righteous.”

When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, his word came to Shemaiah: “They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them; I will grant them some deliverance. My wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.
Whenever the king entered the LORD’s house, the runners came and carried the shields, then returned them to the runners’ guardroom.
Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the LORD’s anger turned away from him and did not destroy him completely. There were also good things in Judah.
He did evil because he had not set his heart on seeking the LORD.
But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not abandoned him. Aaron’s sons serve the LORD as priests, and the Levites attend to their work.

Every morning and evening they burn burnt offerings to the LORD and fragrant incense. They arrange the bread on the pure table and tend the gold lampstand and its lamps to burn every evening. We keep the charge of the LORD our God, but you have abandoned him.
The Israelites were humbled at that time, while Judah’s people grew strong because they relied on the LORD, their ancestors’ God.
He removed the foreign altars and high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles.
He told Judah to seek the LORD, their ancestors’ God, and to carry out the instruction and commandment.
He removed the high places and incense altars from every town in Judah, and the kingdom was quiet under him.
They also struck the livestock camps, captured great numbers of sheep and goats and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.

He went out to meet Asa and said, “Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin! The LORD is with you when you are with him. If you seek him, he will let you find him; if you abandon him, he will abandon you.
They entered a covenant to seek the LORD, their ancestors’ God, with all their heart and all their being.
Anyone who would not seek the LORD, Israel’s God, was to be put to death, whether small or great, man or woman.
The high places were not removed from Israel. Even so, Asa’s heart was whole all his days.
When Baasha heard, he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned his work.
In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his illness grew severe. Even in his illness he did not seek the LORD, but sought the physicians.
The LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the earlier ways of his ancestor David and did not seek the Baals.
His heart took courage in the LORD’s ways. He also removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah.
Israel’s king ordered, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon, the city governor, and Joash, the king’s son.
Tell them, ‘The king says: Put this man in prison and give him scant bread and scant water until I return in peace.’”
Micaiah said, “If you return in peace at all, the LORD has not spoken through me.” Then he added, “Listen, all you peoples!”
Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safely to his house in Jerusalem.
Still, good things have been found in you: you removed the Asherah poles from the land and set your heart on seeking God.”
In Jerusalem too, Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites, priests, and heads of Israel’s ancestral houses to give the LORD’s judgments and settle disputes. They returned to Jerusalem.
He charged them, “This is how you must act: with fear of the LORD, faithfully, and with a whole heart.
Jehoshaphat was afraid. He set himself to seek the LORD and proclaimed a fast throughout Judah.
Judah gathered to seek help from the LORD. They came from every town in Judah to seek the LORD.

After consulting the people, he appointed singers to the LORD, praising in holy splendor as they went ahead of the armed troops. They sang, “Give thanks to the LORD, for his faithful love lasts forever.”
Then every man of Judah and Jerusalem returned joyfully to Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat at their head. The LORD had given them joy over their enemies.
Yet the high places remained, and the people still had not set their hearts on their ancestors’ God.
Edom has remained in revolt against Judah to this day. Libnah also revolted against Jehoram's rule at that time, because he had abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
He also built high places in Judah's hills, led Jerusalem's inhabitants into prostitution, and drove Judah astray.
Ahaziah was forty-two when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for one year. His mother's name was Athaliah, a daughter of Omri.

He returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds they had given him at Ramah when he fought Hazael king of Aram. Azariah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to Jezreel to see Jehoram son of Ahab because he was wounded.
They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherah poles and idols. Wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem because of this guilt.

Then God's Spirit clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood above the people and told them, “This is what God says: Why are you breaking the LORD's commands? You will not prosper. Because you have abandoned the LORD, he has abandoned you.”
The Aramean army came with few men, yet the LORD handed over a very large army to them because Judah had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors. They executed judgment on Joash.
After Amaziah returned from striking down the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of Seir and set them up as his own gods. He bowed before them and burned offerings to them.
You say, ‘Look, I have defeated Edom!’ Your heart has lifted you up to seek glory. Stay home now. Why provoke disaster and bring yourself down, and Judah with you?”
He took all the gold and silver, all the utensils found in God's house under Obed-edom's care, the palace treasures, and hostages. Then he returned to Samaria.
He sacrificed and burned offerings at the high places, on the hills, and under every flourishing tree.
In a single day, Pekah son of Remaliah killed one hundred twenty thousand in Judah, all capable warriors, because they had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors.

But a prophet of the LORD named Oded was there. He went out to meet the army returning to Samaria and said, “The LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah and handed them over to you. Yet you have slaughtered them in a rage that has reached heaven.
Listen to me now. Return the captives you have taken from your own kin, for the LORD's burning anger is against you.”
Some of the Ephraimite leaders confronted those returning from the army: Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai.

The men named above took charge of the captives. From the plunder they clothed everyone who was naked. They gave them clothes and sandals, food and drink, and rubbed them with oil. They put all who were weak on donkeys and brought them to their own kin at Jericho, the City of Palms. Then they returned to Samaria.
In every city of Judah he made high places for burning offerings to other gods. He provoked the LORD, the God of his ancestors, to anger.
Our ancestors were unfaithful and did what was evil in the LORD our God's eyes. They abandoned him, turned their faces away from the LORD's dwelling, and turned their backs on it.

Couriers went throughout Israel and Judah with letters from the king and his officials. At the king's command, they said: “People of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, so that he may return to those of you who remain, who have escaped the grasp of Assyria's kings.

If you return to the LORD, your relatives and children will find compassion with their captors and return to this land. The LORD your God is gracious and compassionate. He will not turn his face from you if you return to him.”
Still, some men from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
everyone who has set his heart on seeking God, the LORD, the God of his ancestors, even without the purification required for the sanctuary.”
The LORD listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.

When all this was over, all the Israelites who were present went out to Judah's cities. They smashed the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and demolished the high places and altars throughout Judah and Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had finished. Then all the Israelites returned to their own property in their cities.
Wasn't it Hezekiah himself who removed his high places and altars and told Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must bow before one altar and burn offerings on it’?

The LORD sent an angel who wiped out every capable warrior, leader, and commander in Assyria's camp. Sennacherib returned to his land with shame on his face. When he entered his god's house, some of his own offspring struck him down there with the sword.
Then Hezekiah humbled himself over his proud heart, and Jerusalem's inhabitants did too. The LORD's wrath did not come upon them during Hezekiah's lifetime.
He rebuilt the high places his father Hezekiah had demolished, set up altars for the Baals, made Asherah poles, and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
In his distress he sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself deeply before the God of his ancestors.
The people still sacrificed at the high places, but only to the LORD their God.

His prayer and how it was answered, all his sin and unfaithfulness, and the places where he built high places and set up Asherah poles and carved images before he humbled himself are written in the records of Hozai.
But he did not humble himself before the LORD as his father Manasseh had. This Amon multiplied his guilt.
Josiah was eight when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for thirty-one years.

In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his ancestor David. In the twelfth year he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, Asherah poles, carved images, and cast images.
he demolished the altars, crushed the Asherah poles and carved images to powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout Israel's land. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

They came to Hilkiah the high priest and handed over the money brought into God's house. The Levite gatekeepers had collected it from Manasseh and Ephraim, from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin. Then they returned to Jerusalem.
They have abandoned me and burned offerings to other gods, provoking me with everything their hands have made. My wrath will pour out on this place and will not be quenched.’

Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and its inhabitants—because you humbled yourself before me, tore your clothes, and wept before me—I too have heard you, declares the LORD.
Jehoiachin was eight when he became king. He reigned in Jerusalem for three months and ten days and did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God. He did not humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah, who spoke the LORD’s words.
He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear an oath by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against returning to the LORD, the God of Israel.
